name: Philip Reed
bio: A Senator and a Representative from Maryland; born near Chestertown, Kent County, Md., in 1760; completed preparatory studies; served in the Revolutionary Army, attaining the rank of captain of infantry; member, Maryland house of delegates, 1787; sheriff of Kent County, Md., 1791-1794; member of the executive council, 1805-1806; elected as a Democratic Republican to the United States Senate in 1806 to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Robert Wright; reelected the same year and served from November 25, 1806, to March 3, 1813; served in the War of 1812; lieutenant colonel of the Twenty-first Regiment, Maryland Militia, in the War of 1812 and lieutenant colonel commandant of the First Regiment, Maryland Militia, in 1814; elected to the Fifteenth Congress (March 4, 1817-March 3, 1819); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Sixteenth Congress in 1818; successfully contested the election of Jeremiah Cosden to the Seventeenth Congress (March 19, 1822-March 3, 1823); died on November 2, 1829, in Huntingtown, Kent County, Md.; interment in the cemetery of Christ Church, Worton, Md., near Chestertown, Md.
